benefits.name: Standard Veteran Property Tax Exemption
benefits.description: New Mexico exempts up to $10,000 of the taxable value of property from taxation for honorably discharged veterans and unmarried surviving spouses who are New Mexico residents. House Bill 47 (2025), implementing a constitutional amendment approved by voters in the 2024 general election, raised this exemption from $4,000 to $10,000 effective the 2025 tax year, with future annual adjustments for inflation. The exemption applies to the veteran's property, including community or joint property of a married couple, and requires continuous active duty service of at least 90 days (unless cut short by a service-connected disability) and an honorable discharge.
benefits.value: $10,000 exemption from taxable property value (adjusted annually for inflation)

otherReqs: Honorable discharge
At least 90 days of continuous active duty (unless cut short by service-connected disability)
New Mexico residency required

application.agency: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department / County Assessor
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge

benefits.name: Proportional Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
benefits.description: Effective the 2026 tax year, New Mexico provides a proportional property tax exemption for veterans with any federal VA service-connected disability rating (previously the exemption required a 100% rating). The exemption equals the veteran's federal disability percentage multiplied by the taxable value of the property remaining after the standard $10,000 veteran exemption is deducted. For example, a veteran with a 70% rating and a home with $150,000 taxable value would first subtract the $10,000 standard exemption (leaving $140,000), then apply the 70% disabled veteran exemption to that remainder ($98,000 exempt), leaving tax owed on only $42,000. The exemption applies to the veteran's principal residence, including joint/community property with a spouse.
benefits.value: Property tax exemption proportional to VA disability rating, applied after the $10,000 standard exemption

otherReqs: VA service-connected disability rating of any percentage (no longer requires 100%)
Applies after the standard $10,000 veteran exemption is deducted
Effective beginning the 2026 tax year

application.agency: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department / County Assessor
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (50%+)
benefits.description: New Mexico issues a free Disabled Veteran license plate (no plate fee or registration fee) for up to two vehicles, including motorcycles, to a veteran with a 50% or greater disability rating incurred while serving in the U.S. Armed Forces. The veteran may elect to add the wheelchair disability symbol to the plate if they would also qualify for a standard disabled-person (HP) plate. New Mexico also offers free plates to Purple Heart recipients, Medal of Honor recipients, Pearl Harbor survivors, and ex-POWs, and a $17 fee-based plate for honorably discharged veterans generally. Applications use Form MVD10353 with DD-214 and supporting documentation, mailed to the MVD Vehicle Services Bureau in Santa Fe.
benefits.value: No fee for plate or registration (50%+ disabled veterans, up to 2 vehicles)

otherReqs: 50% or greater disability rating incurred while serving in the U.S. Armed Forces
Limited to two vehicles (including motorcycles)
DD-214 and supporting documentation required with Form MVD10353

benefits.name: Lifetime & Reduced-Fee Hunting/Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: New Mexico provides a free lifetime small-game hunting and fishing license to veterans with a 100% service-connected disability rating. Veterans with a service-connected disability of a lesser percentage qualify for a reduced-fee $10 small-game and fishing license. Disabled non-resident veterans enrolled in a VA rehabilitation program receive resident-rate licenses. NM-domiciled active-duty, National Guard, or Reserve members may obtain a temporary active-duty fishing/hunting license.
benefits.value: Free lifetime small-game hunting/fishing license (100% disabled); $10 reduced-fee license (partial disability)

otherReqs: 100% service-connected disability rating for the free lifetime license
Lesser disability ratings qualify for the $10 reduced-fee license
Non-resident veterans in VA rehabilitation programs receive resident rates

application.agency: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish / New Mexico Department of Veterans Services

benefits.name: Wartime Veteran Scholarship Fund
benefits.description: New Mexico's Wartime Veteran Scholarship Fund (NMSA 21-21E-3) reimburses public New Mexico institutions of higher education for tuition and required fees for undergraduate, master's, or doctoral coursework for honorably discharged veterans who are New Mexico residents (either at time of entry into service, or after 10+ years of NM residency) and who were awarded a qualifying combat/campaign service medal (e.g., Southwest Asia Service Medal, Global War on Terrorism Service Medal, Iraq Campaign Medal, Afghanistan Campaign Medal, or another medal for U.S. military campaigns/armed conflict after August 1, 1990). Reimbursement is capped at the highest full-time undergraduate tuition rate charged by a public NM institution, with additional reimbursement available for books and supplies. Applications are approved first-come, first-served while funding is available, and require a certified DD-214 showing a qualifying combat/campaign medal and honorable discharge.
benefits.value: Tuition and required fee reimbursement at public NM institutions (capped at highest in-state undergraduate tuition rate), plus books/supplies reimbursement

otherReqs: Honorable discharge required
NM residency at time of entry into service, or 10+ years of NM residency
Must have been awarded a qualifying combat/campaign service medal
Funding is first-come, first-served

application.agency: New Mexico Department of Veterans Services
documentation: Certified DD-214 showing combat/campaign medal and honorable discharge

benefits.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference
benefits.description: New Mexico's State Personnel Office adds 5 points to state civil service examination scores for honorably discharged veterans, and 10 points for veterans with a service-connected disability. The state also offers a Business Tax Credit of up to $1,000 per hire of a recently-returned veteran to private employers, and gives veteran-owned businesses an additional 5% preference in state contract bidding.
benefits.value: 5-point exam score preference for veterans; 10-point preference for service-connected disabled veterans

otherReqs: Honorable discharge required
Disabled veteran tier requires VA service-connected disability documentation

documentation: DD-214 or proof of veteran/disabled veteran status

benefits.name: New Mexico State Veterans' Home
benefits.description: New Mexico operates a 135-bed state veterans home in Truth or Consequences, providing skilled nursing care, memory care, and rehabilitation services. The facility is state-owned and state-operated, coordinates with VA benefits, and is available to eligible veterans who meet state and federal residency and clinical eligibility requirements.
benefits.value: Skilled nursing, memory care, and rehabilitation services at a 135-bed state veterans home

otherReqs: Must have served in the U.S. Armed Forces
State and federal residency and clinical eligibility criteria apply

application.agency: New Mexico Department of Health / New Mexico State Veterans' Home
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service
